title: Fitch Affirms Citigroup Inc. at 'A'/'F1'; Outlook Stable
text:
Fitch Affirms Citigroup Inc. at 'A'/'F1'; Outlook Stable

# Fitch Affirms Citigroup Inc. at 'A'/'F1'; Outlook Stable

Fri 15 Aug, 2025 - 12:14 PM ET

Fitch Ratings - New York - 15 Aug 2025: Fitch Ratings has affirmed Citigroup Inc.'s (Citi) Long- and Short-Term Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) at 'A' and 'F1', respectively, and has affirmed Citi's Viability Rating (VR) at 'a'. The Rating Outlook is Stable. Fitch has also affirmed the IDRs of related entities Citibank, N.A (CBNA), Citibank Canada, Citibank Europe Plc, Citigroup Global Markets Holdings Inc., Citigroup Global Markets Limited, and Citigroup Global Markets, Inc.

In addition, Fitch has affirmed the Government Support Rating assigned to Citi and its primary operating bank subsidiary CBNA at 'ns'. 

### Key Rating Drivers

The ratings reflect progress in Citi's regulatory remediation, as well as improvements to its business profile. Upward assessments across several key rating drivers provide Citi with greater headroom within its current rating.

Operating Environment: Citi has a presence in approximately 95 countries. Its global reach gives Citi a competitive advantage in serving multinational corporations. After the firm's announced strategic refresh in 2021, Citi's consumer banking ambitions were scaled back to focus on its home market of the U.S. Legacy international consumer loans declined to $23 billion at 2Q25, down from $54 billion in 2021. Fitch has affirmed Citi's Operating Environment at 'aa-‌'‌, in line with the U.S.

Strategic Transformation Yields Benefits: Ratings reflect execution to date against its 2022 investor day strategy, including international consumer franchise exits, segment reorganization, organizational simplification, systems investments and improved governance. For the six months ended June 2025, Citi reported double-digit returns on tangible common equity (ROTCE) across all but the Other operating segments, while retaining leadership in its core cash management, securities services, and fixed-income trading businesses. 

Simultaneously, expenses declined 4% in 2024 and are on track to decline further when adjusted for severance and other one-time charges. Despite these gains, Citi's medium-term ROTCE target of 10%-11% would remain below that of higher-rated U.S. peers.

Strengthened Risk Management: Citi has strengthened its risk management capabilities, governance and processes which Fitch expects to facilitate regulatory remediation and reduce operational losses. Exposure to tariff impacts, weakness in commercial real estate and interest rate sensitivity are well-managed and supported by robust underwriting, adequate reserve coverage, and preventive portfolio management.

Stabilized Asset Quality: Citi's asset quality reflects a combination of high-grade corporate loans and a sizable credit card portfolio. Net charge-offs (NCOs) have stabilized as of YE24, and Fitch expects supportive U.S. employment trends and the exit from the Mexican consumer business to help maintain stable credit performance, despite Fitch's base case expectation of a modest rise in unemployment. Reserve coverage is strong at 2.7% of gross loans, with 84% of reserves allocated to consumer exposures.

Positive Operating Leverage: According to Fitch's core earnings and profitability metric of operating profit-to-risk-weighted assets (RWA), Citi's four-year average is the lowest among U.S. peers. However, Citi's ratio improved to 1.8% of risk-weighted assets (RWA) in 1H25 (1.4% for full-year 2024). Fitch expects further gains from business model enhancements, stable expenses, and higher earnings contribution from the Wealth and Banking segments. Expense growth, previously elevated by transformation and one-time charges, has reversed, with costs down in 2024 and further reductions expected over the medium term. Citi's reserve coverage remains robust at 2.7% of gross loans, reflecting prudent provisioning despite CECL-related earnings volatility.

Uncertain Capital Requirements: As of 2Q25, Citi's CET1 ratios of13.5% under the standardized and 11.9% under the advanced approach remained comfortably above regulatory minimums. Planned regulatory changes, including Basel III Endgame enhanced Supplementary Leverage Ratio and Stress Capital Buffer reforms, have yet to be finalized but are expected to have a modest impact on Citi's capital requirements. Citi raised its dividend to $0.60 per share following the 2025 stress test and remains committed to a year-end CET1 target of 13.1%, with share repurchases likely used to maintain capital buffers of at least 100 bp.

Deposit Growth Supports Net Interest Income: Citi's funding profile is underpinned by a large, stable, and diversified deposit base (4.3% U.S. market share as of mid-year 2024) consisting of largely operational cash management accounts (54% of total deposits at 2Q25) and a low loan-to-deposit ratio (53%). 

While reliance on institutional and interest-bearing deposits raises overall costs, deposit growth of 5.7% YTD supports asset repricing and net interest margin expansion. Wholesale funding, comprising 40% of total funding, is well-distributed by maturity and rollover risk is limited. Liquidity remains strong, with average HQLA of $568 billion, a liquidity coverage ratio of 115%, and over $1 trillion in available liquidity funding at 2Q25.

Holdco VR Equalized with Opco: Citi and CBNA's group VR reflects the correlated performance or failure rate between the bank holding company and the bank. As of YE24, Citi's common equity double leverage was 120%.

### Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

-- Regulatory Scrutiny and Remediation Risk: Ratings are predicated on Citi's significant progress in remediating regulatory findings. Therefore, evidence of inadequate remediation progress could prompt a reassessment of rating drivers. These could include further material regulatory findings or significant operational losses;

-- Services Segment: Ratings could be sensitive to a decline in the competitive position of the Services segment, including the Treasury and Trade Solutions business, which Fitch views as fundamental to Citi's business profile; 

-- Credit Losses: A significant increase in credit losses, where impairment charges delay a recovery in operating profit above 1.5% of risk weighted assets (RWA), could prompt negative rating action;

-- Capitalization: A failure to maintain a 50-bp management buffer above Citi's minimum CET1 requirement would be negative for ratings.

### Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Positive Rating Action/Upgrade

-- Improved Profitability: Evidence of a sustainable improvement in run rate operating profit to more than 2% of risk-weighted assets, stronger efficiency, and broad-based revenue growth comparable to higher-rated peers could result in positive rating action; 

-- Regulatory Remediation: Together with stronger profitability, continued progress in remediation of identified outstanding operational weaknesses, such as a lifting of the outstanding 2020 consent orders, would be positive for Fitch's assessment of Citi's risk and business profiles. In addition, reductions in operational, regulatory, and reputational risk would be beneficial.

### OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: KEY RATING DRIVERS

The Short-Term IDR of 'F1' is at the lower of two potential levels that map to the respective Long-Term IDR of Citi and affiliates, reflecting Fitch's assessment of Citi's funding and liquidity profile. 

The long-term deposit rating of 'AA-‌' assigned to CBNA is one notch higher than CBNA's Long-Term IDR to reflect superior recovery prospects in the event of a default given depositor preference in the U.S. Fitch assigns CBNA a short-term deposit rating of 'F1+' which corresponds with CBNA's long-term deposit rating.

Senior unsecured debt is rated in line with the respective issuing entities' IDRs, as Fitch views a default on these obligations as equivalent to a default of the issuing entity.

Derivative counterparty ratings (DCRs) of Citigroup, CBNA, Citigroup Global Markets Limited, and Citigroup Global Markets, Inc. are equalized with their Long-Term IDRs because they have no definitive preferential status over other senior obligations in a resolution scenario. Therefore, the DCR ratings will move in line with the companies' respective IDRs. These ratings have been assigned because the companies are either engaged in significant derivatives activity or are counterparties to Fitch-rated structured finance transactions.

Subordinated debt and other hybrid capital issued by Citi are notched down from the group VR in accordance with Fitch's assessment of each instrument's respective non-performance and relative loss severity risk profiles, which vary considerably. Citi's subordinated debt rating reflects the baseline notching for loss severity of two notches from the VR. 

Citi's preferred stock rating is four notches from its VR, which encompasses two notches for non-performance and two notches for loss severity. The preferred stock ratings of Citigroup Capital III and Citigroup Capital XIII are also four notches from Citi's VR. 

### OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: RATING SENSITIVITIES

The Short-Term IDR would be sensitive to a change in the respective entities' Long-Term IDRs, or a change in Citi's funding and liquidity profile. Senior debt ratings, deposit ratings and DCRs, where assigned, are primarily sensitive to changes in the respective issuers' Long-Term IDRs. 

Subordinated debt and other hybrid ratings are primarily sensitive to any change in Citi's VR. 

### SUBSIDIARIES & AFFILIATES: KEY RATING DRIVERS

Material Domestic Subsidiaries: The Long-Term IDRs of the U.S. operating entities — CBNA, Citigroup Global Markets Holdings Inc., and Citigroup Global Markets Inc. (U.S. broker dealer) — are one notch higher than Citi's Long-Term IDR. This reflects Fitch's belief that the U.S. single-point-of-entry resolution regime, the implementation of total loss-absorbing capacity requirements for U.S. global systemically important banks (G-SIBs), and the presence of substantial external debt buffers reduce the default risk of the domestic operating subsidiaries' senior liabilities relative to holding company senior debt.

Fitch has assigned a Shareholder Support Rating (SSR) to Citigroup Global Markets Holdings Inc. and Citigroup Global Markets Inc. of 'a', in line with Citi's Long-Term IDR of 'A'. Per criteria, Long-Term IDRs can be assigned above the SSR and/or VR based on protection to creditors provided by intra-group resources, as detailed in a group's resolution plan.

Material International Subsidiaries: Per Fitch's "Bank Rating Criteria," the Long-Term IDRs of Citibank Europe Plc and Citigroup Global Markets Limited (international broker dealer) have also been notched above Citi's Long-Term IDR. This decision is based on accepted resolution plans that identify these key foreign subsidiaries as beneficiaries of intra-group resources, among other factors.

Fitch has assigned to Citigroup Global Markets Limited an SSR of 'a', in line with Citi's Long-Term IDR of 'A', in accordance with criteria. Fitch has assigned to Citibank Europe Plc an SSR of 'a+', in line with the Long-Term IDR of its direct parent, Citibank, N.A.

Other Subsidiary: Although not designated as a material legal entity, Citibank Canada's activities are integral to the group's business and strategy in Fitch's view. Its Long-Term IDR is equalized with Citi's Long-Term IDR of 'A', reflecting Fitch's view of a high likelihood of support by the parent in case of need. Fitch has assigned to Citibank Canada an SSR of 'a' in line with the VR of its parent, Citibank, N.A.

### SUBSIDIARIES AND AFFILIATES: RATING SENSITIVITIES

Material Domestic Subsidiaries' Rating Sensitivity: The Long-Term IDRs of Citi's material domestic subsidiaries would be sensitive to a change in Citi's Long-Term IDR.
